newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kurd charged in Germany as top PKK official.
newsitem.headline: Kurd charged in Germany as top PKK official.

text.p: German prosecutors said on Monday they had charged a man they believe to be a top official of the outlawed Kurdistan Workers' Party's (PKK) in Europe with membership of a terrorist organisation and arson.

The Federal Prosecutors' Office said in a statement the Turkish citizen of Kurdish origin named only as Murat E. had acted as treasurer in Europe since 1995 for the PKK, which is fighting for an independent state in southeastern Turkey.

It said he was a member of the party's Europe-based executive and had occupied this senior position over the last few years -- during a campaign of arson attacks on Turkish targets by suspected PKK activists across Germany.
Prosecutors accused him of helping to carry out numerous arson attacks and other serious offences in 1995 and 1996.
Murat E., 37, has been in custody since June last year.
More than 21,000 people have died during the PKK's 12-year-old campaign in Turkey.
